rationale: Branch B (diagnose graph-construction sensitivity) selected. Primary-method (greedy) evidence: repair activated on 10/30 rows (33.3%; 33.3% of graphs were cyclic pre-repair -- almost entirely the multi-provider aggregate graph, per per_graph breakdown), but 0/10 activated cases changed nDCG at all (0.0% nonzero-among-activated, below the 20% trigger). This is 'nearly invariant outcomes': repair is structurally real (it removes edges, changes graph shape) but never once altered the resulting Copeland ranking's nDCG in this pilot -- consistent with cycles being confined to document pairs/positions that do not affect the top-of-ranking order nDCG measures at pool_size=6, top-relevance-only pool construction. Scaling this exact construction (Branch A) would only add more zero-information rows. Localized analysis (Branch C) presupposes repair sometimes visibly matters at some grain, which was not observed at any grain here. Branch B (vary pool size/diversity/aggregation/orientation/sparsity) is the evidence-supported choice.
